idiom_name: async transform/middleware: Promise.all lookups + spread merge
implementation_notes: JavaScript realizes the enricher as an async function (or middleware) that awaits the resource and merges the result into the message with spread/Object.assign - the Enricher and DataSource roles collapse into one function plus a client. Promise.all runs several independent lookups for a single message concurrently, and a Map-based TTL cache or the messaging library's middleware chain absorbs repeats; in Node the resource call is asynchronous, so nothing blocks the event loop. Keep the client behind an injectable object so tests run without the resource.
pitfalls: A Map used as a cache never expires and never bounds: a long-lived consumer leaks every key it ever saw.
Promise.all rejects on the first failed lookup and discards the successful ones; use allSettled when partial enrichment is acceptable.
Spreading a nested object copies the reference, not the subtree, so later mutations of msg.address still show up in the 'enriched' copy.
